A 403 CSRF failure after moving the form into a partial usually means the POST no longer carries the token: either the partial dropped {% csrf_token %} from inside the form, or it's rendered without the request context so the tag comes out empty. The fix is to put {% csrf_token %} inside the form in the partial, or send the token on every htmx request with hx-headers='{"X-CSRFToken": "{{ csrf_token }}"}' on the body. Action: look at the partial and how the view renders it in trailmix; paste them if you'd rather check yourself.

Use useLayoutEffect when you must measure or change the DOM before the browser paints so the user never sees an in-between frame: positioning a tooltip from getBoundingClientRect, or setting scroll position right after content changes. For everything else, such as fetching, subscriptions and logging, use useEffect, since it doesn't block painting. If you server render, useLayoutEffect warns on the server, so guard it. `docker compose up -d` creates the containers, networks and volumes if they don't exist (recreating containers whose config changed) and starts them detached. `docker compose start` only starts containers that already exist and are stopped, without creating anything or applying config changes. HTTP/1.1 keep-alive only reuses a TCP connection for the next request, but responses still come back one at a time per connection, so browsers open several connections to get parallelism. HTTP/2 multiplexing lets many requests and responses interleave concurrently as separate streams over one connection, and it adds header compression. Caveat: HTTP/2 still has TCP-level head-of-line blocking on packet loss, which HTTP/3 addresses. Action: none needed.

The JSON round trip only keeps what JSON can represent: Dates become strings, Maps and Sets become empty objects, undefined and functions disappear, and circular references throw. structuredClone keeps Dates, Maps, Sets and typed arrays and handles cycles, though it still can't copy functions or class prototypes. So prefer structuredClone unless you deliberately want a JSON-safe copy. Action: point me at the line the reviewer flagged and I'll check whether it's safe to swap.
